newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka shares end up, profit-taking slows rises.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka shares end up, profit-taking slows rises.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks ended higher on buying by local retail investors on Friday but profit-taking limited gains, brokers said.
The all share index closed 3.04 points higher at 608.04. Gainers outnumbered losers by 29 to 11.
"The index would have gained more if not for profit-taking by retailers, mainly rich locals, who had been instrumental in moving the index up," said Shanil Perera of Lanka Securities.
Brokers said they saw some foreign selling too. "Some foreign investors are using the recent gains in the index to cut exposure," said Ruan Dayananda of Asia Securities.
Brokers said bargain hunting and profit-taking alternated throughout Friday's trading dominated by retail investors.

Turnover was a moderate 33.89 million rupees on 1.7 million shares, supported by local buying of 564,000 Blue Diamonds Jewellery which ended unchanged at 12.50 rupees. Among actively traded shares was Seylan Bank which rose 75 cents to 26.75.
Brokers said some foreign buyers were forced to the sidelines due to the lack of availability among blue chips.
Three Acres rose 6.25 rupees to 34.75 on news of the company's expansion into piggery and retail business.
